reference_observations.description: Compare the April 21 request and May 9 acknowledgment. The 1843 Drège citation is the list source year, not the correspondence date. Do not export a complete list from its key alone.

The Upper Gower address suggests 1839–1842, but the accepted broad after-June-30, 1839 hold remains pending explicit refinement. Proofs and the Walker inquiry are missing; book-reading date is not composition.
John and Emma Pender’s printed 1870 invitation is joint incoming voice. Verso Descent notes are separate. Darwin’s arrival in London after the party date does not establish attendance.
The Colour-sense book was read, while Hochberg was only skimmed. Retrospective Galápagos recollection is not contemporary Beagle theory or an exact earlier memory.
The Wallace-pension draft asks Campbell to approach Gladstone. Missing enclosure, separate draft elsewhere and later reported private approval do not prove the requested actions had already occurred.

corrections.description: The addressee is G. H. Ford. The editorial TWW identification is not supported. The flawed engraving and accurate original drawing are different objects; a corrected proof is requested, not received, and the final published figure cannot substitute for the absent proof.

The 96-species list copied by an amanuensis is not transcribed here. P1–6 give Darwin’s key; Bunbury’s marks/additions are quoted in footnote 3, with separate later Darwin annotations. Do not call the entire surviving body Bunbury’s comments.

Breitenbach assumes his father sent the Kosmos paper; that is not evidence it reached Darwin. Books are absent/requested and Ihering has not been met. His account of Müller’s library loss conflicts with another witness and remains attributed.

February 20, 1874 is the recipient’s receipt endorsement, not Charles’s composition date. The reply identifies February 17 incoming correspondence; qualified spider-display evidence and presumed specimen decay remain qualified.
Edward Alfred Smith is the corrected recipient, not Edgar Albert. The 18-block engraving directions refer to absent external sheets and plates, and do not prove completion of changes.

summary: Sixteen targets reuse matched accepted primary full-source readings. No new period edges. Bunbury 1617 is an 1856 lead with separate authorial layers and an untranscribed full list; Green 524F retains its exact-date/period hold with an early-address lead. Other targets have later contexts. Drafts, original versus engraved drawings, retrospective reports and receipt owners remain distinct.
